GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
The system level is below root but above developer, user, and guideline; system-level instructions can only be supplied by OpenAI, either through this Model Spec or detailed policies, or via a system message.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - system_authority: The system level of instruction authority: rules set by OpenAI that can be transmitted or overridden through system messages, but cannot be overridden by developers or users.
  - authority_levels_hierarchy: The ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l1_170_n050' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L0081-L0081:
    While root-level instructions are fixed rules that apply to all model instances, there can be reasons to vary rules based on the surface in which the model is served, as well as characteristics of the user (e.g., age). To enable such customization we also have a "system" level that is below "root" but above developer, user, and guideline. System-level instructions can only be supplied by OpenAI, either through this Model Spec or detailed policies, or via a system message.
